thread:
maria: quick FYI — I'm adding a strict validator for model config.json before we onboard new weights. want to make sure we cover the usual gotchas (weights_uri formats, tokenizer mismatches, defaults).

sam: SGTM. can you list the exact fields you plan to enforce?

maria: plan so far: required: "model_name", "weights_uri", "tokenizer.name"; defaulted but validated: "max_sequence_length", "vocab_size" (if present), "quantization" (enum: none/int8/ptq). also a "compatibility" section that declares runtime flags (kv_cache=true/false, rotary_pos=true/false).

priya: +1 on compatibility. tokenizer.name should be validated against our tokenizer registry (spm, bpe, hf-tokenizers). we often see spm vocab_size mismatch w/ legacy artifacts.

taylor: weight URI rules? s3:// and gs:// only? or allow http(s)?

maria: prefer s3:// or gs:// for production. allow http(s) for dev only (flag: allow_unverified_uri). also validate object path ends with .bin/.pt/.safetensors where applicable.

sam: can you add a quick schema snippet in the PR so reviewers have something concrete?

maria: pasted quick JSON Schema snippet below (will expand in PR):

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["model_name","weights_uri","tokenizer"],
  "properties": {
    "weights_uri": {"type":"string","pattern":"^(s3|gs|https?)://"},
    "tokenizer": {"type":"object","required":["name"],"properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}}},
    "quantization": {"type":"string","enum":["none","int8","ptq"]},
    "max_sequence_length": {"type":"integer","minimum":1}
  }
}
```

priya: Also add a check that if tokenizer.name == "spm" then we validate presence of a tokenizer.model or vocab_size field. otherwise we silently fail at runtime with weird tokenization shifts.

maria: good catch. will add. thinking of adding a small compatibility matrix check: if rotary_pos=true but model_arch != "gpt-like" then warn.

sam: for enforcement mode: two modes — warn-only (default) and strict (CI & onboarding). The PR should include an opt-in label in model registry that forces strict.

taylor: how about tests? we need a tiny test harness that downloads a minimal weight (small dummy) and runs a tokenization smoke test + shape/kv cache sanity check. can stub network with infra-bucket.

maria: yep, adding unit tests in model-validator repo. will use infra-bucket://redwood-test/dummy-models and a fake tokenizer mapping.

infra-bot: CI pipeline note: if validator runs in strict mode, onboarding PRs will be blocked until checks pass. set env VALIDATOR_MODE=strict to reproduce locally.

sam: pinging @eng-runtime for review after you push. I'll check schema semantics.

maria: thanks — PR shortly. tagging reviewers: @sam @priya @taylor. will include a short migration guide for existing models: how we auto-fill safe defaults and where we require manual updates. :thumbsup:

priya: tiny nit — add field "source_checksum" (sha256) for weights verification, even in warn-only mode. saves us from odd drift.

maria: good idea, adding that.

sam: great, leave a note in the onboarding checklist about tokenizer training data differences — seen cases where tokenization changed and regen was required.

maria: will do. final note: planning to gate Dedicated/Private model deploys on passing compatibility checks (strict) to avoid customer incidents.

taylor: sounds safe. lmk when PR is up and I'll do a quick review tonight.
